## Booleans
The boolean operators (== || && !) only work for primitive types. It compares what's stored in bits, which for primitive types is its value, but reference types store addresses. It is comparing if the addresses not the actual value.

No strings, use `.equals()`

**SHORT CIRCUITING**:
If the boolean statement already equates to true, the computer stops evaluating the || statement.
Be careful what order you put your conditions in, in evaluation operators and in if else statements or similar.

Important to keep in mind that this happens in EVERY evaluation, even if there's a lot of nested and multiple evaluations going on

## Ifs, Else ifs, and Elsas
Without brackets, an if statement will only run the first line under it. If there is an else if or else statement after an if with no brackets, it will throw a syntax error if there is more than one line of code separating it from the else/else if because it doesn't know you started an if statement

if (evaluation) 
expression
another expression <---- SYNTAX ERROR IT DOESN’T KNOW THE IF EXISTS
else if (evaluation

This would throw a syntax error

if (evaluation)
expression
else if (evaluation)

This would compile but it's a bug waiting to happen, don't do it just use brackets

Remember that else does not use () for evaluation.

There's three kinds of else/else if/if statements and they're called suites.
1. if / if/ if
2. if / else (note you can put else if statements in here but it will end with an else)
3. if / else if / else if (it does not end in else)

**Fizz Buzz: (very common type of interview question)**

If a number is divisible by 2, print fizz
if a number is divisible by 3, print buzz
if a number is divisible by both, print fizz buzz

```
int num = 12;
if (num % 2 == 0) {

System.out.print("fizz");
}
if (num % 3 == 0) {
System.out.print("buzz");
}
```
